# S204 — Engine follows relay v11 process rules: gate close timing and [AFTER LAND] Check lines

ork's engine settles when a v11 gate round closes with its verdict (owner question Q1), treats a Check line marked `[AFTER LAND]` as deferred to land (approval card and role prompts), and records which v11 process rules it already meets. The non-blocker owner question rule is a separate slice (`engine-v11-rules-2`).

**Findings:** S198 preflight 2026-10-30: owner split the engine rules out of S198 · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-10-30** — From S198 review (2026-10-30): a v11 gate step is closed with the report's verdict at internal/engine/round.go:400, before a TriageGate shape error (round.go:471-481) or an Owner needed question (round.go:493-505) can pause the round, so the ledger can show pass for a round the engine did not accept; a retry then records a second gate round that slicer's gate_rounds/with_verdict counts (../slicer/src/slicer/relayrun.py:973-982) would count twice (retry behaviour not traced). Decide whether such a round closes with its verdict (now) or without one.

**2026-11-01** — Open owner questions from the 2026-10-31 spec drafting. Ask the owner before the relay starts; the spec waits on these.

Q1 (drafter C; suggested adj key relay.gate-verdict): does a v11 gate round close with its verdict before the engine accepts the round?
What the drafter traced: internal/engine/round.go:439-462: for a v11 gate the step is closed with "--phase done --verdict pass or fail" right after the report is read, before TriageGate (:477), before the "## Owner needed" pause (:500-509) and before the [owner blocker] hold (:513-530). CheckReport returns no report on a shape error, so a report with a bad first line already closes without a verdict (TestV11GateWithoutAVerdictLineClosesWithoutOne). After a pause, Answer or Retry runs the gate again as a new attempt with a new ledger step (round.go:226-233 names the attempt, stepStart at :605-622 opens the step), and the engine counts the slice's gate FAILs only for accepted rounds (internal/engine/states.go:554-584, rec.Fails++). slicer's _measure counts every gate-role lane step as a gate round regardless of phase and verdict (../slicer/src/slicer/relayrun.py:973-982), so the retried gate is two gate rounds in both options. What the verdict changes: with the verdict on the first step, with_verdict counts it and gate_fails counts it when it says fail although ork wrote no "Review FAIL" note and did not send the slice back; without it, gates.by_proxy counts the round (:1052) and gate_fails counts it only when an implementer fix round follows it (:977-982), which a retried gate is not. So the "twice" in the S198 note is two rounds, not one verdict counted twice; the real difference is a verdict in the ledger for a round ork did not act on.
Options: (a) keep: close with the verdict as the report says it; the ledger shows a PASS or FAIL for a round that then paused. (b) Close with the verdict only for a round the engine accepts (the one that returns outcome ok true, round.go:534); a round paused for a shape error, an owner question or a blocker finding closes done with no verdict, and the retried gate carries it. (c) Close such a round "--phase fail --reason ..." with no verdict; the drafter does not recommend it: fail means the role's process failed, and the run tree draws it as a failed step.
Drafter recommendation: (b): the ledger verdict matches what ork acted on.
Waits: S204 Implement step 3 and the "Gate close" tests. Other S204 steps do not wait.

Q2 (drafter C): how are v11 rules 1 and 2 recorded?
Rule 1, "a small fix round is checked and gated in one pass by the read-only role that raised its findings": ork's fix round goes to checks and then the gate, which resumes the reviewer's session (internal/engine/states.go:164-176,523-531); there is no second review round. Pinned by TestReviewFindingsStartAFixRoundAndTheResumedReviewerGatesIt (internal/engine/engine_test.go:361).
Rule 2, "a clean merge of main is regated by the one-pass small-fix check on the merge diff": ork merges main in, renders, re-runs the project check command and "slicer check", then fast-forwards, with no role round (internal/engine/land.go:110-175); the ledger run has already ended at the finish step, so a regate round could not be recorded (S153).
Options: (a) document rule 1 as met and rule 2 as a deviation in docs/design.md and docs/orchestrator-parity.md; (b) build a one-pass gate round on the merge diff in land.go with no ledger step: a separate M, E-class slice.
Drafter recommendation: (a): nothing to build, and it matches how ork already runs.
Waits: the wording of two docs rows in S204 step 7; no code.

Q3 (drafter C): does ork run an [AFTER LAND] Check line itself at landing?
Options: (a) no: the approval card lists each such line as "deferred to land: ..." (already in state later), and the owner runs it after landing; ork runs only the project check command, never a slice's Check lines, and a line may be prose. (b) Yes, for a line that is one backticked command: run it in the main checkout after the fast-forward, and a failure pauses the slice. A separate slice.
Drafter recommendation: (a).
Waits: S204 Implement step 4 is written for (a); under (b) report and stop.

## Why

Split out of S198 on 2026-10-30 (owner, interactive) and re-scoped on 2026-10-31 after tracing each rule against the code. `slicer ai relay` and `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` print relay v11 today. This slice covers the rules below; the non-blocker owner question rule (S204's fourth bullet) is its own slice because it adds ledger calls, a record field and a read-back.

Rule by rule, as traced against HEAD of main on 2026-10-31:

- **A small fix round is checked and gated in one pass by the read-only role that raised its findings** (`slicer ai relay-orchestrator`, Gate bullet). ork already runs no second review round after the first: `checks` jumps to `beforeGate` once a reviewer record exists (`internal/engine/states.go:164-176`), and the gate resumes the reviewer's session (`internal/engine/states.go:530-531`, brief text `states.go:525-526`). `TestReviewFindingsStartAFixRoundAndTheResumedReviewerGatesIt` (`internal/engine/engine_test.go:361`) pins it. No code change. Whether this counts as "the role that raised the findings" is Q2; this slice only records the current behavior in the docs.
- **A clean merge of main is regated by the one-pass small-fix check on the merge diff** (`slicer ai relay`, Order and Land step 6). ork merges main in, renders, re-runs the project check command and `slicer check`, then fast-forwards with no role round (`internal/engine/land.go:110-175`). The ledger run has already ended at the finish step (`internal/engine/states.go:663-689`), and relay-run refuses steps after that (S153, `internal/engine/land_test.go:617`). No code change here; Q2 asks whether to document this as a deviation or build a regate round.
- **A Check line marked `[AFTER LAND]` is deferred to Land step 6** (`slicer ai relay-orchestrator`, Every brief). The implementer and the gate do not run it, and the finish step does not wait for it. ork's prompts say nothing about it, so an implementer may try to run a line that needs a slice that has not landed. The approval card lists only `[HUMAN CHECK]` bullets (`internal/engine/approval.go:22-37`), so a plain `- [AFTER LAND] ...` line never reaches the owner, and a `[HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] ...` line shows as an ordinary open check that blocks approval until ticked (`internal/engine/engine.go:390`). This slice fixes both (Q3 asks whether ork should run such lines itself; this slice does not).
- **`relay-run list` `counts.roles` counts lane steps only** (`slicer ai relay`; `../slicer/src/slicer/relayrun.py:417-436`). ork decodes `Counts.Roles` (`internal/slicercli/types.go:166`) but never reads it: the only users of `Counts` read `Steps`, `Running` and `Waiting` (`internal/tui/overview.go:396-402,1267`, `internal/tui/runtree.go:390`, `internal/daemon/handlers.go:409`). No behavior change; the field comment says what it counts.
- **A gate round is closed with its verdict.** S198 sends it (`internal/engine/round.go:439-462`). The step closes with the report's verdict before the engine knows whether it accepts the round. A gate report whose `TriageGate` fails (`round.go:477`), whose `## Owner needed` asks something (`round.go:500-509`), or that carries an `[owner blocker]` finding (`round.go:513-530`) pauses the slice with the verdict already recorded. On retry or answer the gate runs again as a new attempt with a new ledger step (`internal/engine/round.go:226-233`, `stepStart` at `round.go:605-622`). Traced in slicer: `_measure` counts every gate-role lane step as a gate round, whatever its phase (`../slicer/src/slicer/relayrun.py:973-982`), so a retried gate is two gate rounds either way. What differs is the verdict. With the verdict on the first step, `with_verdict` counts it and `gate_fails` counts it when it says `fail`, although ork did not accept the round and wrote no `Review FAIL` note; the step's `verdict` shows a PASS the engine never acted on. With no verdict, `by_proxy` counts the round (`gates.by_proxy = gate_rounds - with_verdict`, `relayrun.py:1052`) and `gate_fails` counts it only if an implementer fix round follows it, which a retried gate is not (`relayrun.py:977-982`). The choice is Q1.

Three owner questions gate parts of this slice. Q1 (gate close timing): (a) keep the close as now, (b) close with the verdict only for a round the engine accepts, (c) close a paused round as `fail`; the draft recommends (b). Q2 (rules 1 and 2): (a) document rule 1 as met and rule 2 as a deviation, (b) build a one-pass gate round on a clean merge as its own slice; the draft recommends (a). Q3 (`[AFTER LAND]`): (a) list the line on the card for the owner, (b) run single-command lines at landing as its own slice; the draft recommends (a). The outer session records the answers as an `Owner decisions` paragraph on this slice before the worktree is cut (`slicer ai relay`, Setup). Until Q1 is answered, step 3 of Implement is not started; the rest follows the recommended answers.
